hints: A bridge cannot be crossed both ways after it is oriented.
A connected undirected graph without bridges admits a strongly connected orientation.
Orient DFS tree edges downward and back edges toward ancestors.
analogy: Every DFS branch needs a return road to an ancestor so directed travel can get back up.
example: A triangle can be oriented 1->2->3->1; a single edge cannot be made strongly connected.
algorithm: Run DFS from one vertex, orienting tree edges from parent to child and non-tree edges from descendant to ancestor. Compute discovery and low values. If any vertex is unvisited or any tree edge has low[child]>discovery[parent], print IMPOSSIBLE; otherwise print the assigned directions.
correctness: A bridge or disconnected graph makes strong connectivity impossible. With no bridge, every DFS subtree has a back edge to its parent or an ancestor, so every vertex can travel upward to the root, while tree edges allow the root to reach every vertex.
complexity: For n vertices and m edges, O(n+m) time and O(n+m) space.
